\title{Macro-Heavy Benchmark: Neural Architecture Convergence}
\author{Charlie Macro \and Dana Dense}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We study the convergence of overparameterized neural networks in $\real^d$.
Our analysis leverages the neural tangent kernel $\mH$ to establish
that gradient descent on the empirical loss $\loss(\vw)$ converges to a
global minimum at rate $O(1/t)$ when $\norm{\vw_0 - \vw^*} \leq R$.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

Let $\dataset = \{(\vx_i, \vy_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ with $\vx_i \in \real^d$
and $\vy_i \in \real$.  We consider a two-layer network
$f(\vx; \mW) = \mA \relu(\mW \vx)$ where $\mW \in \real^{m \times d}$
and $\mA \in \real^{1 \times m}$.

The empirical loss is:
\[
\loss(\mW) = \frac{1}{2n} \sum_{i=1}^n \norm{f(\vx_i; \mW) - \vy_i}^2
\]

We define the NTK matrix $\mH \in \real^{n \times n}$ by:
\[
\mH_{ij} = \inner{\nabla_{\mW} f(\vx_i; \mW)}{\nabla_{\mW} f(\vx_j; \mW)}
\]

\section{Assumptions and Setup}

\begin{enumerate}
\item The data satisfies $\norm{\vx_i} = 1$ for all $i$ and $\abs{\vy_i} \leq B$.
\item The width satisfies $m \geq \ceil{n^6 / \lambda_0^4}$ where $\lambda_0 = \lambda_{\min}(\mH^{(0)}) > 0$.
\item Initialization: $\mW^{(0)}_{jk} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 2/m)$ for all $j, k$.
\end{enumerate}

Under these conditions, the expected loss decomposes as:
\[
\expect[\loss(\mW^{(t)})] = \expect[\loss(\mW^{(0)})] \cdot \left(1 - \frac{\eta \lambda_0}{2}\right)^t + \frac{\eta \sigma^2}{2 \lambda_0}
\]

The gradient update is:
\[
\mW^{(t+1)} = \mW^{(t)} - \eta \nabla_{\mW} \loss(\mW^{(t)})
\]

\section{Main Theorems}

\begin{theorem}[Linear convergence]
\label{thm:linear}
Under Assumptions 1--3, gradient descent with $\eta \leq 2 / \norm{\mH^{(0)}}$ satisfies:
\[
\norm{\vy - f(\mW^{(t)})}^2 \leq \left(1 - \frac{\eta \lambda_0}{2}\right)^t \norm{\vy - f(\mW^{(0)})}^2
\]
where $f(\mW)_i = f(\vx_i; \mW)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define $\vz^{(t)} = \vy - f(\mW^{(t)})$.  By Taylor expansion around $\mW^{(t)}$:
\begin{align}
\norm{\vz^{(t+1)}}^2
&= \norm{\vz^{(t)} - \eta \mH^{(t)} \vz^{(t)}}^2 \\
&= \norm{(\mA - \eta \mH^{(t)}) \vz^{(t)}}^2 \\
&\leq \left(1 - \eta \lambda_0\right)^2 \norm{\vz^{(t)}}^2 \\
&\leq \left(1 - \frac{\eta \lambda_0}{2}\right) \norm{\vz^{(t)}}^2
\end{align}
where $\mA = \mB - \diag(\tr(\mH))$ and the last step uses $\eta \leq 2/\norm{\mH}$.
Telescoping completes the proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Kernel stability]
\label{lem:kernel}
For $m \geq \ceil{n^6 / \lambda_0^4}$, the kernel matrix satisfies
$\norm{\mH^{(t)} - \mH^{(0)}} \leq \lambda_0 / 4$ for all $t \leq T$.
\end{lemma}

\section{KL Divergence Bound}

For generalization we bound the $\dkl{\prob_{\model}}{\prob_{\dataset}}$:
\[
\dkl{\prob_{\model}}{\prob_{\dataset}}
\leq \frac{1}{2\sigma^2} \sum_{i=1}^n \norm{f(\vx_i; \mW^*) - \vy_i}^2 + \frac{d}{2} \log\frac{\sigma^2}{\sigma_0^2}
\]

The optimal parameters are $\vw^* = \argmin_{\vw \in \real^d} \loss(\vw)$
and the predictive distribution uses $\softmax$ for classification tasks.

The floor function $\floor{m / n}$ gives the effective overparameterization
ratio and we need $\floor{m/n} \geq n^5$.

See Theorem~\ref{thm:linear} and Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel}.

\section{Conclusion}

We showed linear convergence for overparameterized networks with
width $m = O(n^6 / \lambda_0^4)$.  The analysis extends to $\argmax$
objectives and deeper architectures via recursive NTK computation.
